bio: O Grove is a peninsula with stunning coves of fine white sand that overlooks the entrance to the Arousa estuary dotted with shellfish beds. This is the setting for Culler de Pau, in a valley full of cornfields and small orchards, where chef Javier Olleros has his family home and where he runs this business with his wife Amaranta Rodríguez, with an ethos that is underpinned by concerns about issues such as obesity, the climate crisis and the fast food culture. In the minimalist-style dining room, adorned with stunning works of sculpture that showcase the inner light that shines within us, discover “zero-mile” cooking on three menus (Ronsel, Marexada and Descuberta) that reflect a commitment to the environment and to the Atlantic.
